title: What happens if a Kafka broker runs out of disk space?
shortTitle: What happens if a Kafka broker runs out of disk space?

s1_definition.oneliner: A full broker disk takes its partitions offline for writes and stalls replication, so you prevent it with retention, monitoring, quotas, and capacity, and recover by freeing space or adding disk.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **IO errors** -- when a log directory fills up, the broker cannot append records or write index entries, so it logs IO exceptions and marks the directory offline.
- **Partition unavailability** -- partitions whose leaders are on the full broker become unavailable for writes, and producers get `NotEnoughReplicas` or timeout errors.
- **Replication stall** -- follower replicas on the full broker cannot persist fetched data and fall out of the in-sync replica set, reducing durability.
- **Prevention** -- set `retention.ms` or `retention.bytes` per topic, monitor disk usage with alerts at 70-80%, use producer quotas, and consider tiered storage.
- **Recovery** -- reduce retention to let the cleaner free space, add disk or brokers, and let replicas catch up and rejoin the ISR.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine the clerk's desk at National Bank of India is completely covered in ledgers with no room left to write. The clerk cannot record any new transaction, so new entries get rejected and pile up at the counter. The backup clerks who copy the ledgers also cannot keep up, so their copies fall behind. The fix is to archive old ledgers off the desk regularly, watch the desk's fullness and get warned before it overflows, and get a bigger desk or more clerks before the rush.

  Producer quotas                 ──► Prevent runaway writes
  Tiered storage                  ──► Local disk stays small
  Separate data volume            ──► OS survives disk full

sections.s6_takeaway:
When a Kafka broker's log directory fills up, the broker can no longer append records or write index files, so it logs IO errors, marks that log directory offline, and takes its hosted partitions out of service. For partitions whose leader was on the full broker, writes fail and producers get rejected. Follower replicas on the full broker fall out of the in-sync replica set, reducing durability across the cluster.

I prevent it with retention settings, disk monitoring with alerts at seventy to eighty percent, producer quotas, and tiered storage for high-retention topics. For recovery I never hand-delete segment files; instead I reduce retention to let the cleaner free space, add disk or brokers, and let the recovered replicas catch up and rejoin the ISR.

In my National Bank of India project, a surge plus a retention misconfiguration once filled one broker. We recovered by temporarily cutting retention and adding capacity, and we hardened the setup by separating the data volume from the OS volume, balancing partitions evenly, and adopting tiered storage.

Remember one sentence: a full broker disk takes partitions offline and erodes durability, so prevent it with retention, monitoring, quotas, and separate data volumes.

---

keyPoints: A full broker disk causes IO errors that take partitions offline for writes and stall replication.
Follower replicas on the full broker fall out of the ISR, reducing durability across the cluster.
Producers get NotEnoughReplicasException or timeout errors for affected partitions.
Prevent with per-topic retention settings, disk monitoring with alerts at 70-80%, and producer quotas.
Recover by reducing retention to free space, never by manually deleting segment files.
Separate the Kafka data volume from the OS volume so a full data disk does not crash the OS.
Tiered storage prevents this for high-retention topics by keeping only recent segments locally.
